doc.title: Rebecca Kilgore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Taking up guitar and jazz guitar lessons
summary: She began with folk guitar, played chords to Billie Holiday sheet music, and took a year of jazz guitar lessons in Boston.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: And you took up the guitar in high school?

Yeah I actually took up the folk guitar. I wanted to play like Judy Collins and Joan Baez. And I taught myself how to play those three chords and stuff. And then I guess it was when I discovered the Billie Holiday stuff I was intrigued by that and I would go buy the sheet music and play the chords while I would sing along, for my own amusement. And that’s where I took it.
More than three chords in that music.
Yeah a lot more. And it even made me take guitar lessons. I took a year of jazz guitar lessons in Boston and that’s where I got the foundation for the chordal stuff that I do now.
But your musical tastes have not been confined to just, say, the jazz world either, right?
